title: Ethiopian Okra Stew
community: Southern Ethiopia — the okra fasting stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Okra Stew — fresh okra cooked with tomato, onion, garlic, and a touch of berbere. A southern Ethiopian fasting dish — the okra's natural mucilage thickens the sauce into something surprisingly rich.
longDesc: Okra stew is particularly popular in southern Ethiopia where okra grows abundantly in the warmer climate. The okra's natural thickening agent produces a sauce of remarkable body.
ingredients: 400g fresh okra — trimmed, sliced into rounds
steps: Heat oil. Cook onion until golden.
Add garlic, berbere, and turmeric. Stir 30 seconds.
chefTips: Dry okra before cutting — excess moisture increases sliminess.
Handle gently — do not over-stir or it becomes very mucilaginous.
cookingScience: Okra's mucilage is composed of galactan oligosaccharides — a type of soluble fibre that forms a gel when heated with water. This gel thickens the stew naturally. Less stirring means less mucilage release; some is desirable for sauce body, too much is unpleasant.
sustainabilityTips: Okra is extremely drought-tolerant — grows in areas where other vegetables cannot.
servedWith: As a southern Ethiopian fasting side
healthBenefits: High in vitamin C and K.
culturalNote: Okra stew is the southern Ethiopian contribution to the fasting platter — bringing a different texture and thickening quality from the highlands' legume-based stews.
